about.title: Gonzales Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Gonzales is a small, close-knit Monterey County city surrounded by farmland, and everyday equipment — from agricultural tools and machinery parts to household appliances and vehicle components used along corridors like US-101 and Alta Street — can cause serious harm when something is built, designed, or labeled wrong. California generally treats these cases under strict liability, meaning an injured person typically doesn't need to prove the manufacturer was negligent, only that the product was defective and that the defect caused harm. That can apply to the maker, distributor, or even the local retailer who sold it. If you or someone you love was hurt by a defective product in Gonzales, holding onto the item, packaging, and any receipts matters. We're a product liability team ready to review your claim on contingency, so there's no upfront cost while your options are evaluated.

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Your Path
items.desc: Because California often applies strict liability to defective products, you may not need to prove the manufacturer was careless — just that the defect existed and caused harm.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and even retailers can potentially be held liable, which widens the pool of parties we can investigate.

items.title: Preserving the Product Matters Early
items.desc: Since the product itself is often central evidence, contacting us soon after an injury helps ensure it's kept intact and properly documented.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California product liability law frequently relies on strict liability, meaning you generally need to show the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury, rather than proving carelessness. Our team can evaluate which legal theory best fits your situation.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Keep it exactly as it was at the time of the injury, including any packaging, instructions, or parts that broke off. This is especially important in a smaller community like Gonzales, where the product may still be in use locally and evidence can be easy to lose or repair before it's reviewed.

items.question: Do you charge anything for a case review?
items.answer: No. We offer free case reviews, and we typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.

items.question: Can I still pursue a claim if the product was bought outside Gonzales?
items.answer: Possibly, since California law can apply based on where the injury occurred or where you reside, not just where the product was purchased. Our team can review the specifics, including any connection to local retailers or distributors near US-101 or Fanoe Road.
